results.summary_before: This is a small SPI slave that receives 6-bit messages and drives the 7-segment display on the Tiny Tapeout carrier board. The first two bits of each message form a command that turns the decimal point on or off, and the remaining four bits select the digit to display; malformed commands turn the decimal point on with the rest of the display blank. The SPI signals SCLK, SS and MOSI are mapped to the clock and two input pins, and the seven segments plus decimal point appear on the eight outputs. It requires the carrier board's seven-segment display and a microcontroller to act as SPI master.

The first two bits of each message form a command that turns the decimal point on or off, and the remaining four bits select the digit to display; malformed commands turn the decimal point on with the rest of the display blank. The SPI signals SCLK, SS and MOSI are mapped to the clock and two input pins, and the seven segments plus decimal point appear on the eight outputs. It requires the carrier board's seven-segment display and a microcontroller to act as SPI master.

results.summary_before: This design is a 115200 baud UART transceiver that stores received characters in a 16-byte buffer and asynchronously drives four HPDL-1414 alphanumeric LED display modules. When the buffer fills, existing characters shift left to make room, a blinking cursor shows the input position, and Ctrl-H performs a backspace for editing. Testing is done by connecting a computer or microcontroller at 115200 baud, sending ASCII characters, and observing them on the HPDL-1414 modules. It requires the external HPDL-1414 PMOD module and uses a 12 MHz clock.
